key_insight: The paper shows that neural operators can be constructed directly from numerical discretization schemes, especially finite element and finite difference methods, bridging operator learning with classical PDE solvers.
engineering_relevance: This provides a more interpretable and parameter-efficient way to build surrogate models for PDE-based engineering simulations, with convergence guarantees from numerical analysis.
method: Approximate or learn finite element basis functions with neural networks.
Unroll finite-difference time stepping into iterative neural modules.
Use numerical analysis to derive error bounds and convergence estimates for the resulting neural operator.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports numerical experiments showing reduced error and improved parameter efficiency compared with general neural operator constructions.
watch_item: The approach may depend on the chosen discretization and PDE class, so transfer to different meshes, boundary conditions, or highly nonlinear systems may require retraining or redesign.
paper_title: Numerical Neural Operator: Connection Between Numerical Analysis and the Operator Learning and Building Discretized Neural Operators from Finite Element Methods
